Hunting With Dogs

By: ALTYDVRYSTAAT PRODUCTIONS | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We go inside the inner circle of the dark world of dog poachers and hunters. Blanche investigates...

Unique Selling Point:
We go inside the inner circle of the dark world of dog poachers and hunters.
Carte Blanche investigates...


Summary:
We explore the three different types of dog hunting groups:
1. The pot hunters. Economically disadvantaged people who use dogs and
traps to hunt for food.
2. Social hunters. People who travel from as far as Johannesburg to hunt
with friends using dogs.
3. Gamblers. This is very problematic. Large groups, there can be as much as
more than a hundred hunters at a time, gather on a pre-determined farm. Each
hunter has between one and five dogs. Every hunter puts a predetermined
amount in the kitty. This varies between R1000 and R10 000 per hunter. The
rules are also decided. Sometimes the hunter whose dog gets the first antelope
will win all the money. Other times it is the owner of the dog that takes down the
biggest antelope.

Further information:
We have people who are willing to talk, but they are very scared. So their
identities will have to be concealed. There are literally zero footage. I found only
one farmer with some pictures of hunters and their dogs as well as weaponry
confiscated from hunters. If you are keen, this story will be built using these
photos and anonymous interviews.

Press Release:


Hunting with Dogs

In a controversial practise that is escalating across the country, participants in so-called taxi hunts transport their highly-prized hunting dogs to participate in illegal hunts that are publicised far and wide on social media. Although hunting with dogs has been outlawed in South Africa, it is practiced widely and has landowners up in arms as livestock or game is caught and killed, indiscriminately, by vicious dogs. Carte Blanche travels to Northern KwaZulu-Natal where the devastation caused is fuelling tensions in an already tense relationship between landowners and hunters.

Producer: AltydVrystaat Productions | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

Script:


Illegal Hunting With Dogs -- FINAL


Hunters walking with dogs...

V/O
It’s a common sight in rural KwaZulu-Natal…. Men walking with their dogs...
07:05:29 [Hunter 1]: We call it hunting.
07:05:31 [Hunter 2]: Yes, we call it hunting. We are hunting using the dogs.

V/O
These men live in Dumbe, just north of Paulpietersburg and like many others, they venture out early mornings onto neighbouring farmlands to hunt with their dogs.
Hunter 07:06:36 [Hunter 2]: We use speedhounds. Sometimes we use crossbreeds of speed hound and greyhound or speedhound and saluki or whippet, but the most popular dogs right now are speed hounds...

V/O
But this morning’s hunt has cost them dearly, their one prize hunting dog was severely injured...
7:08:26 [Hunter 1]: It’s not easy for it to participate again because it has damaged its knee and the knee is everything. 07:08:29
Sdumo 07:15:07
[Claire]: How much do the dogs cost the owners? How much is one dog?
(12”)
07:15:10
[Sdumo]: Ey, ey, ey, 60 or 70. Not less than R45 000. I think R15 000 is for a puppy.
V/O

TITLE
Silverton “Sdumo” Maseko Having grown up in the area, Sdumo Maseko knows how valuable the dogs are.

07:15:18 [Claire]: Where do they get so much money for the dogs?
07:15:20 [Sdumo]: These people own cattle. In this area people still pay lobola with cattle. I can exchange 3 cows for one dog.

LINK Hunting with dogs has a long history in South Africa. Today it is practised outside the law, fuelling tensions between rural communities, game reserves and private landowners.

Sdumo 07:13:46 [Sdumo]: That is the big problem that we face is the coexistence with the South African private landowners.

07:13:51
V/O
Maseko says there are more than a thousand men regularly hunting with dogs in the district.
Sdumo
07:13:51 [Sdumo]: In reality, it’s wrong for a dog to go onto private owned land and eat their animals but the private landowners are also not innocent. (57)
07:14:02 [Sdumo]: Some will allow dog hunting but... 07:14:03:27
07:14:07 [Sdumo]: Others don’t agree. 07:14:08:52
07:14:14:46 [Sdumo]: Naturally, in that kind of situation, related to dog hunting, there will be conflict.

Frans de Jager
Clip0058.MXF Hier’s boere wat afgegaan het van 70 elande op hulle grond afgegaan het dat daar nou basies so 11 elande oor is in ’n kwessie van die laaste drie jaar.
Some farmers in this area went from 70 Eland on their farms down to 11 over the past three years. (Subtitle)

V/O
Drone Frans de Jager is an anti-poaching expert with years of experience protecting rhinos in the Kruger National Park… but the escalating impacts of hunting with dogs means that he now spends his days patrolling private farmlands in the remotest parts of KZN...

Frans de Jager 0:19:29:12 - 00:20:03:12
Your situation is very tense at the moment because as as they push, you know, anyone is a farmer, you farms because he loves the animals. They don't like to see the animals die. They don't want the fences to be cut. They don't want these guys to burn the field, to chase out the game.

V/O
For De Jager and his team, tracking and apprehending trespassing hunters and their dogs is a full-time job.
Frans de Jager 00:06:47:19 - 00:07:13:03
At the moment, we can say that under estimation that we have in our area here at least 200 to 250 dogs hunting every weekend.

V/O
Hunting is a way of life, say the men who do not want to be named… occasionally it will be for meat, but mostly it’s a hobby.

Hunters 07:05:47
[Hunter 1]: We are just passing time, so we do not find ourselves doing bad things (no good/crime/ etc). We just go out and play this game.
07:06:01
[Hunter 2]:
When we see an antelope we release the dogs just to see which one will be faster. Even if they don’t kill the antelope, it’s just for us to see which dog is faster. Then the winner collects the money.

V/O
What they refer to as a game, is in actual fact a well-organised sport. Each event has rules and a captain to play referee.

Hunters 07:07:19
[Hunter2]: He’s the one who usually solves conflicts because he rarely goes to the woods with us. He oversees what is happening from a clear hilltop. So he sees which dog caught the antelope first.

V/O
Depending on the rules of the day the winner could be the dog that catches the first animal, or the biggest antelope. ..and there's good money to be made, especially at the larger competitions...
Sdumo Maseko 07:13:01 [Sdumo]: There is a local level around Dumbe. Maybe the joining fee is R100. Then the competition value is an estimated, R3000. Then there is a district competition maybe, [the value is] R45 000 because the joining fee is more than R5000.

Andre Symington 0:14:30:08 - 00:14:30:23
It is so lucrative nowadays to be part of it, it's like horse racing, but just on a smaller scale, people are winning. People are making money. It's a social event.

V/O
Senior state prosecutor Andre Symington is based in Vryheid and an expert in environmental crimes like organised hunting with dogs.

Andre Symington 00:06:29:01 - 00:06:58:11
These hunts are being promoted on social media, on Facebook, and they are then attended by quite a lot of people, quite literally, overwhelming the owners, the farmers, the community members on their own property.

LINK Clip 0028.mxf (17:36:55:15)
(12”)
Taxi hunts are primarily for sport or for gambling. Outsiders come from as far as Johannesburg with taxi’s filled with hunting dogs that are hungry and ready to catch whatever they can.

Herman de Wet
Ready, steady, go - Mpumalanga Hunters (17”) 00:02:26:07 - 00:02:58:27
They form up in a formation, each dog on a leash and they move through an area. If any antelope or something jumps up, he blows the whistle and they release the dogs.

V/O
Herman de Wet chairs TLU South Africa’s KZN Branch. He farms with cattle and sheep, which he refers to as take-aways because they are so easy to hunt.
Herman de Wet (11”) 00:20:11:11 - 00:20:29:08
A group of dogs like that if they start chasing sheep, you could find out that 20, 30, 40 sheep has been killed in the process.

V/O
One of the big problems is that hunting with dogs is non-selective…

Herman de Wet (22”) 00:13:06:16 - 00:13:22:23
You cannot tell the dog only catch Impala, only catch a duiker. That dog is bred to hunt. And it doesn't matter what jumps up, they will chase it.
Frans de Jager 00:13:04:17 - 00:13:26:05
There’s like the oribi, the steenbok, the aardwolf… There's a whole lot of endangered species and that species will just go more extinct if we do not counter these guys.

LINK Clip 0025.mxf (17:35:17:23)

Take two:
(9”)
A quick search on social media and you’ll find various hunting groups advertising hunts and showing off their dog’s skills.

V/O (7”)
Cellphone videos shared by members show the variety of wildlife taken out and the brutality of the kills.
Herman de Wet (20”)
00:03:37:15 - 00:04:03:09
They will isolate a kudu from the rest of the group and they will chase it until it physically steps on his tongue. Now I say that is the cruelest of cruelty.

V/O
For De Wet and others the answer lies in legalising dog racing, which will give the men the opportunity to pit their dogs against each other, without the need to kill… but according to the NSPCA both hunting with dogs, and racing dogs is in contravention of our animal welfare legislation.
Sdumo (14”)

07:14:46 [Sdumo]: Why is there always noise around dog racing but they don’t say much about horse racing?
(13”)

07:14:54 [Sdumo]: Yes, it’s painful because there is a loss. When people go hunting, we call it “giving”/”an offering”.

Sdumo (15”)
07:14:18 [Claire]: No matter how you do it, whether you’re alone or in a group, whether it a game. The law says that dog hunting is not allowed.

(11”)
07:14:23 [Sdumo]: We were never told that. What is lacking is for South African Police to come and educate people on what is legal and illegal. Because people think that what they are doing is legal.

V/O

Besides breaking the law by trespassing and illegally hunting valuable game and livestock, farmers are also having to contend with vandalism and damage to infrastructure.
Herman de Wet 00:13:52:15 - 00:13:57:12
Every Monday on my farm, I must fix fences. A Kudu can jump over six foot fence by just standing and with the spring in the leg, jump over a six-foot fence. But if a dog has chased that animal for two kilometres or a kilometre, it can't jump over a cattle fence, which is one point four metres. Then it runs through the fence.
Andre Symington (12”)

00:06:58:22 - 00:07:10:01
What rights do the farmers have then once people are trespassing on their land to hunt with dogs?
(12”)
00:07:10:09 - 00:07:11:06
Right, the first thing that the farmer have to do is, of course, ask for the assistance of the police.

V/O
But the police are not necessarily trained in environmental crimes, and Symington adds that old legislation and a dated penalty system means that those caught illegally hunting with dogs are rarely prosecuted effectively.
Andre Symington Claire: Has anyone been prosecuted? Have people gone to jail?
Uh, gone to jail, no… prosecutions yes...
If you look at the fines at the end of the day and if you look at the court time that the prosecutors have. Sometimes they have to make the decision; is it worth it to spend so much time, so much energy, and what do you get at the end of the day? … a slap on the wrist...

Frans de Jager (8”)
00:18:52:09 - 00:19:10:03
I think if you make an example of one of these groups, the rest will say, listen here, we must think twice before we go and kill these animals with the dogs.

V/O
But for Maseko and the hunters the official nod from the local chief means that the hunt is allowed, and that’s the law they abide by.
Sdumo We need to get chiefs and kings involved because people know that once they are involved, things automatically become formal. When you go out the chief will ask, “Where are you going?” We will say, “We are going to hunt using dogs”. Then the chief can assert, “That is illegal!” Yes.

PROMO 1 While hunting with dogs is illegal in South Africa, it continues to escalate and in northern KwaZulu-Natal where the tensions it causes between communities and private landowners is reaching boiling point.

PROMO 2 Hunting with dogs is escalating in many parts of the country despite being illegal. Is this hunting for the pot where food is scarce…or is it all about the thrill of the chase?

PROMO 3 An innocent traditional pastime fuelled by poverty... or a brutal, self-serving gamblers’ game? We investigate the escalating incidents of hunting with dogs in rural KwaZulu-Natal.

Herman de Wet (11”) 00:20:11:11 - 00:20:29:08 A group of dogs like that if they start chasing sheep, you could find out that 20, 30, 40 sheep has been killed in the process. V/O One of the big problems is that hunting with dogs is non-selective… Herman de Wet (22”) 00:13:06:16 - 00:13:22:23 You cannot tell the dog only catch Impala, only catch a duiker. That dog is bred to hunt. And it doesn't matter what jumps up, they will chase it. Frans de Jager 00:13:04:17 - 00:13:26:05 There’s like the oribi, the steenbok, the aardwolf… There's a whole lot of endangered species and that species will just go more extinct if we do not counter these guys. LINK Clip 0025.mxf (17:35:17:23) Take two: (9”) A quick search on social media and you’ll find various hunting groups advertising hunts and showing off their dog’s skills. V/O (7”) Cellphone videos shared by members show the variety of wildlife taken out and the brutality of the kills. Herman de Wet (20”) 00:03:37:15 - 00:04:03:09 They will isolate a kudu from the rest of the group and they will chase it until it physically steps on his tongue. Now I say that is the cruelest of cruelty. V/O For De Wet and others the answer lies in legalising dog racing, which will give the men the opportunity to pit their dogs against each other, without the need to kill… but according to the NSPCA both hunting with dogs, and racing dogs is in contravention of our animal welfare legislation. Sdumo (14”) 07:14:46 [Sdumo]: Why is there always noise around dog racing but they don’t say much about horse racing? (13”) 07:14:54 [Sdumo]: Yes, it’s painful because there is a loss. When people go hunting, we call it “giving”/”an offering”. Sdumo (15”) 07:14:18 [Claire]: No matter how you do it, whether you’re alone or in a group, whether it a game. The law says that dog hunting is not allowed. (11”) 07:14:23 [Sdumo]: We were never told that. What is lacking is for South African Police to come and educate people on what is legal and illegal. Because people think that what they are doing is legal. V/O Besides breaking the law by trespassing and illegally hunting valuable game and livestock, farmers are also having to contend with vandalism and damage to infrastructure. Herman de Wet 00:13:52:15 - 00:13:57:12 Every Monday on my farm, I must fix fences. A Kudu can jump over six foot fence by just standing and with the spring in the leg, jump over a six-foot fence. But if a dog has chased that animal for two kilometres or a kilometre, it can't jump over a cattle fence, which is one point four metres. Then it runs through the fence. Andre Symington (12”) 00:06:58:22 - 00:07:10:01 What rights do the farmers have then once people are trespassing on their land to hunt with dogs? (12”) 00:07:10:09 - 00:07:11:06 Right, the first thing that the farmer have to do is, of course, ask for the assistance of the police. V/O But the police are not necessarily trained in environmental crimes, and Symington adds that old legislation and a dated penalty system means that those caught illegally hunting with dogs are rarely prosecuted effectively. Andre Symington Claire: Has anyone been prosecuted? Have people gone to jail? Uh, gone to jail, no… prosecutions yes... If you look at the fines at the end of the day and if you look at the court time that the prosecutors have. Sometimes they have to make the decision; is it worth it to spend so much time, so much energy, and what do you get at the end of the day? … a slap on the wrist... Frans de Jager (8”) 00:18:52:09 - 00:19:10:03 I think if you make an example of one of these groups, the rest will say, listen here, we must think twice before we go and kill these animals with the dogs. V/O But for Maseko and the hunters the official nod from the local chief means that the hunt is allowed, and that’s the law they abide by. Sdumo We need to get chiefs and kings involved because people know that once they are involved, things automatically become formal. When you go out the chief will ask, “Where are you going?” We will say, “We are going to hunt using dogs”. Then the chief can assert, “That is illegal!” Yes. PROMO 1 While hunting with dogs is illegal in South Africa, it continues to escalate and in northern KwaZulu-Natal where the tensions it causes between communities and private landowners is reaching boiling point. PROMO 2 Hunting with dogs is escalating in many parts of the country despite being illegal. Is this hunting for the pot where food is scarce…or is it all about the thrill of the chase? PROMO 3 An innocent traditional pastime fuelled by poverty... or a brutal, self-serving gamblers’ game? We investigate the escalating incidents of hunting with dogs in rural KwaZulu-Natal.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We go inside the inner circle of the dark world of dog poachers and hunters. Blanche investigates...
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We go inside the inner circle of the dark world of dog poachers and hunters. Carte Blanche investigates...
metadata.Summary: We explore the three different types of dog hunting groups: 1. The pot hunters. Economically disadvantaged people who use dogs and traps to hunt for food. 2. Social hunters. People who travel from as far as Johannesburg to hunt with friends using dogs. 3. Gamblers. This is very problematic. Large groups, there can be as much as more than a hundred hunters at a time, gather on a pre-determined farm. Each hunter has between one and five dogs. Every hunter puts a predetermined amount in the kitty. This varies between R1000 and R10 000 per hunter. The rules are also decided. Sometimes the hunter whose dog gets the first antelope will win all the money. Other times it is the owner of the dog that takes down the biggest antelope.
metadata.Further information: We have people who are willing to talk, but they are very scared. So their identities will have to be concealed. There are literally zero footage. I found only one farmer with some pictures of hunters and their dogs as well as weaponry confiscated from hunters. If you are keen, this story will be built using these photos and anonymous interviews.
